# 4 Maccabees Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Eleazar's First Confrontation with Antiochus

---

**1** When Antiochus realized that the people were actively resisting his plans and holding fast to their ancestral law, he commanded his soldiers to round up every Hebrew and force them to eat food prohibited by the law.

**2** Anyone who refused was to be tortured to death.

**3** Among the many who were brought in was a man named Eleazar — a priest, a scholar of the law, well advanced in years, and well known to the king's courtiers for his intellectual reputation.

**4** When Antiochus saw him, he said:

**5** Old man, before your torture begins I want to give you a chance: eat the meat and save your life.

**6** I respect your age and your white hair — but I find it hard to call you wise when you cling to these ideas.

**7** What exactly is it that compels you to practice this Jewish religion? It strips you of the natural pleasures of life.

**8** Frankly, I think it is foolish to deny yourself harmless pleasures.

**9** You would be better off following the example of your own people who have already adopted our way of life.

**10** I urge you to let go of your old prejudices and embrace a more enlightened perspective.

**11** Take pity on your old age. Show some respect for your white hair.

**12** And consider: if there really is some divine power watching over your religion, surely he will forgive anything done under compulsion.

**13** But if you persist in these old-fashioned Jewish scruples, you will be executed as a warning to others.

**14** At these words, Antiochus had his guards bring in the torture instruments.

**15** Eleazar looked at them as though they were not even there, lifted his eyes toward heaven, and asked to speak.

**16** Permission was granted, and he addressed the gathering:

**17** Antiochus, we who are convinced that the divine law governs our lives find no compulsion stronger than obedience to that law.

**18** We therefore judge it wrong to transgress the law in any way whatsoever.

**19** Even if our law were not truly divine — even if we had only mistakenly believed it to be so — it would still be dishonorable for us to compromise our devotion to God.

**20** Do not think it is a small thing if we eat the defiling food.

**21** Transgressing the law is equally serious whether it involves small or great matters — because in both cases the law is equally dishonored.

**22** You mock our philosophy as if we did not really live by it. But our law has shaped us in self-control — mastering our pleasures and desires; in courage — enduring every pain willingly; in justice — treating everyone fairly; and in godliness — worshiping the one true God with genuine reverence.

**23** That is why we do not eat food that defiles us.

**24** We believe the law was given by God, and so we trust that God — the Creator of all things — acts with compassion toward us. He allows what is good for our souls and forbids what harms them.

**25** The tyrant, hearing these words, seemed to regard them as nonsense. He dismissed them with contempt and ordered the tortures to begin.
